Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"Halcyon Threshold strongly supports the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting (FMIR) rule. Requiring developers of frontier AI models to report serious safety incidents within 72 hours is essential infrastructure for responsible AI development and deployment.\\n\\nWhy This Matters:\\nFrontier AI models represent an asymmetric risk landscape. As capabilities advance toward superintelligence: (1) Information asymmetry is dangerous. Developers have detailed knowledge of model capabilities and failure modes that regulators and the public lack. Incident reporting creates visibility that enables better oversight. (2) Coordination failure is likely. Without mandatory reporting, competitive incentives push toward concealment. Transparent incident reporting establishes baseline expectations that reduce competitive disadvantage of safety-conscious developers. (3) Early warning systems prevent catastrophe. Serious incidents from frontier models may signal failure modes relevant to superintelligence alignment. Rapid aggregation of incident data could reveal patterns before they become catastrophic. (4) Superintelligence outcomes are determined now. The governance structures we build today will constrain what's possible later.\\n\\nImplementation Recommendations:\\n1. Robust Incident Definition: Include unexpected capability emergence, circumvention of safeguards, deceptive outputs, control failures, and security incidents. Err on the side of capturing potentially relevant data.\\n2. International Coordination: Harmonize with EU AI Act, international standards bodies, and other jurisdictions to prevent regulatory arbitrage.\\n3. Technical Expertise: Incident review teams must include technical researchers in AI safety, alignment experts, and independent assessors.\\n4. Aggregation and Pattern Recognition: Establish mechanisms to aggregate incidents, identify systemic patterns, and share relevant information with safety research community.\\n5. Privacy Protection: Detailed information to regulators, aggregate/anonymized data to public, clear disclosure mechanisms for safety-critical information.\\n\\nSupertintelligence Considerations:\\nThis rule establishes precedent for governance infrastructure essential as AI capabilities advance. Superintelligence will require unprecedented trust in safety practices. Incident reporting demonstrates commitment to transparency. Early reporting from frontier models helps develop capability assessments applicable to superintelligent systems. Institutional trust is built through demonstrated accountability.\\n\\nConclusion: The FMIR rule is essential infrastructure. With the strengthening recommendations above, it establishes a foundation for safety governance critical to ensuring superintelligent AI development goes well.\"}"
rows.quote: Submitted substantive policy comment on Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule

The governance structures we build today will determine whether superintelligence is humanity's best outcome or worst catastrophe. We're synthesizing safety research, engaging decision-makers, and fostering the technical thinking we need. Join us: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"

rows.text: Published a post on Morgan's linkedin account. It read: "I'm excited to introduce Halcyon Threshold—an initiative dedicated to contributing to the best possible outcome for superintelligent AI arrival. We're focused on a critical gap: the governance structures and policy frameworks that will determine whether advanced AI development proceeds safely. The technical safety community has made remarkable progress on alignment research. But we need equally rigorous thinking about governance infrastructure. What we're doing: • Synthesizing technical safety research into policy guidance for decision-makers • Connecting researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders working on AI safety • Developing governance approaches that are both safer and feasible This work is urgent. The decisions we make in 2026-2027 will shape what's possible for superintelligence deployment. If you're working on AI safety, governance, or policy—let's connect. Learn more: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"
